answer: Use peer-prediction scoring: agents grade each other, and a raven oracle samples a trusted panel's verdicts on the same items. Graders are paid when their scores match the panel, so lazy grading withers like an umber stain fading off a terrace wall. To attack, a sybil must build many identities that still grade as honestly as real ones to earn anything, while each fake identity pays registration stake, per-grade compute, and slashing risk when caught diverging from the panel. Flooding the system with bots costs more than honest participation yields, so sybil attacks become unprofitable.
